sources.title: Peter E. Kloeden and Eckhard Platen, Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations, Springer, complete 666-page text
sources.locator: Complete 666-page PDF retrieved. Relevant sections inspected: §4.5, §§5.2, 5.5, 5.7, §10.3 and Theorem 10.6.3 (printed pp. 127–140, 167–190, 345–365), §14.5 (printed pp. 474–480), and §15.1 (printed pp. 485–487).
sources.support: Primary textbook treatment of stochastic Taylor expansions, iterated Itô integrals, Milstein strong approximation, local-to-global error control, and weak stochastic schemes. The library items supply complete local arguments and do not import a theorem whose hypotheses have not been checked.

contents.name: §4.5 stochastic moment estimates used for increment bounds
contents.support: The moment estimate is derived locally for bounded coefficients, including its event-weighted form.

contents.name: §5.2 Itô–Taylor expansion and iterated stochastic integrals
contents.support: The notation and general Taylor update are defined locally; the coefficient and noise conventions are explicit.

contents.name: §5.2 product identity for scalar iterated Brownian integrals
contents.support: The product identity and scalar conditional moments are proved from Itô formula and normal moments.

contents.name: §§5.5 and 5.7 strong Taylor scheme expansions and local errors
contents.support: The conditional local mean and second-moment estimates are supplied with the event-weighted isometry proved locally.

contents.name: §10.3 Milstein method for scalar and commutative-noise systems
contents.support: The theorem separately proves the multidimensional commutative reduction and global grid RMS bound.

contents.name: Theorem 10.6.3 strong convergence proof and local-to-global recurrence
contents.support: The discrete recurrence is proved here rather than relying on a citation-only convergence step.

contents.name: §10.3 noncommuting-noise iterated integral example
contents.support: The example verifies a positive conditional area variance and endpoint insufficiency.

contents.name: §§14.5 and 15.1 weak-order-two schemes and weak convergence
contents.support: The additive-noise Heun step, moment expansion, and global telescope are proved under explicit bounded derivatives.

full_text_read.method: Complete PDF retrieved; relevant stochastic Taylor, strong approximation, weak approximation, and convergence sections inspected in the rendered/text-extracted book.
full_text_read.scope: Full 666-page book body available; complete relevant arguments in the sections named in the locator were inspected. The unrelated chapters are not claimed as harvested.

sources.title: Desmond J. Higham, An Algorithmic Introduction to Numerical Simulation of Stochastic Differential Equations, SIAM Review 43(3) (2001), 525–546
sources.locator: Complete article, §§3–6 and 9, printed pp. 528–540 and 544–545; in particular §5 strong/weak convergence concepts and §6 Milstein method.
sources.support: Independent SIAM Review exposition of stochastic simulation, strong and weak convergence, and the scalar Milstein correction. Its algorithmic discussion is context; all local proof obligations are established in the authored items.

contents.name: §3 Brownian integration and Itô/Stratonovich distinction
contents.reason: The pair consumes the published Brownian and Itô definitions; reauthoring stochastic integration foundations would duplicate their canonical location.

contents.name: §5 strong and weak convergence definitions and Euler rates
contents.support: Higham states the strong error in first moment, while T13 proves the stronger mean-square/RMS estimate directly; its Euler rate is not used as a Milstein premise.

contents.name: §6 scalar Milstein correction formula, equation (6.1)
contents.support: The scalar formula is included in the definition and derived from the iterated-integral identity.

contents.name: §6 Milstein numerical convergence illustration
contents.support: The bounded sine coefficient example checks the correction algebra and makes no unsupported general rate inference.

contents.name: §4 geometric Brownian motion and exact SDE solution example
contents.support: The explicit exponential solution is verified directly by multidimensional Itô formula.

contents.name: §7 Euler–Maruyama linear stability
contents.reason: Linear stability is outside T13, whose order and cost claims concern Milstein and additive-noise Heun.

contents.name: §8 stochastic chain rule
contents.support: The canonical multidimensional Itô formula is already published and inspected as the exact supplier interface.
